definition.stop: Available search slots >= 1 or completion of an explanatory model.
definition.uncertainty: The theoretical threshold where a research question ceases to be generative remains speculative.

assumptions: Computational agents can estimate the variance of future discovery outcomes.
Cost of investigation can be quantified through resource expenditure or time.
Novel path-dependencies can be detected through internal state monitoring.
definition.falsification: Agents fail to abandon dead-end questions despite high resource costs and zero observed novelty, indicating a sunk-cost bias that exceeds internal thresholding capabilities.
definition.statement: An intelligence should abandon a starting question when the variance of potential discovery outcomes falls below the computational cost of continued investigation, provided that no novel path-dependencies have been identified.
definition.uncertainty: The precise metric for 'potential discovery outcomes' is currently heuristic-based and lacks a formal, universally accepted computational definition.
